summary: TechCrunch reports on a 60 Minutes interview with Michael Lewis, whose book "Going Infinite" about Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) debuts as SBF's fraud trial begins in Manhattan Federal Court. Lewis recounted that SBF considered a roughly $5 billion payment to get Trump not to run again, and described SBF's rise, celebrity deals and political dealings. The article also gathers critical reactions and notes that the interview leaves unclear whether it flatters or condemns SBF, with the jury to decide how criminal his intentions were.
one_line: Michael Lewis told 60 Minutes SBF floated a $5 billion figure to keep Trump from running, as SBF's FTX fraud trial and Lewis's book launch.
key_facts: Sam Bankman-Fried's trial in Manhattan Federal Court begins Tuesday; he is accused of orchestrating "one of the biggest financial frauds in American history" via the multibillion-dollar collapse of FTX.
SBF has pleaded not guilty to some seven charges of fraud and conspiracy.
Michael Lewis's book "Going Infinite" about SBF is set to debut on the first day of the trial.
Lewis says he was introduced to SBF in early 2021 by a friend who wanted to back FTX and asked Lewis to "evaluate his character"; both lived in Berkeley.
Lewis and SBF met more than 100 times over two years.
Lewis said SBF went from nothing to $22.5 billion in 18 months and was the richest person in the world under 30.
SBF raised some $2 billion, including $1 billion in 2021, from backers including Sequoia, Temasek and Tiger Global.
Tom Brady was reportedly paid $55 million and Steph Curry $35 million in FTX marketing deals; Anna Wintour asked SBF to sponsor the Met Costume Ball.
Trades on FTX climbed up to $15 billion/day.
Lewis said a plan existed to buy off Trump so he would not run again, with a figure of $5 billion "kicking around"; SBF was never sure whether it came from Trump.
Lewis said SBF met Mitch McConnell to discuss funding candidates to offset Trump's influence in the Republican Party, and also looked to back Democratic candidates.
Ayelet Noff of Sliced Brand said SBF was "in way over his head" and pushed back crypto adoption by at least a year or two.
Critics including Ryan Selkis, Dan Held and Tobi Lutke criticized the 60 Minutes coverage and Lewis's defense of SBF.
